benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Eased to about $91.98 on 12 Nov (Trading Economics), down roughly 0.8% on the day and about 3% from $94.62 a week earlier (Nov 5). Reuters reported Ukrainian strikes have cut Russia's oil refining capacity by about 30% since late October, and UKMTO logged a fresh tanker strike near the Strait of Hormuz on Nov 10, even as Iraq's reported Hormuz understanding and sanctioned-tanker license talks keep weighing on the risk premium.

note: Oil eased on 12 November while gas firmed: Brent fell to about $91.98/bbl and WTI to about $85.72/bbl, down roughly 1% on the day, while TTF rose to about €89.81/MWh. Reuters reported Ukrainian strikes have cut Russia's oil refining capacity by about 30% since late October, citing industry sources, and UKMTO reported a fresh tanker strike near the Strait of Hormuz on Nov 10 alongside an attack on an ADNOC vessel in the Gulf. Qatar's LNG loadings have climbed to roughly half the pre-war pace (Bloomberg/Kpler), even as Poland's Orlen became the first QatarEnergy customer to cancel a long-term LNG contract over the disruption.
